pull.title: wallet: Update tx chain state during loading during AttachChain instead of before
pull.body:
When loading a wallet, updating the state based on the chain data prior to `AttachChain` results in some blocks being missed, which leads to inconsistent state information that can cause assertion failures. Moving the state updating inside of `AttachChain` after the chain notifications handler has been attached ensures that the state will always be up to date with the tip that the wallet is tracking.

Fixes #34599

ACK 18bc686c6e97fb5522a93412240ddca99057f1b7

Reviewed the change and tested locally.

Moving the tx state update out of `LoadToWallet()` makes sense to me. During DB
load, the wallet may already have a chain pointer, but it is not yet registered
for chain notifications. In `AttachChain()`, notifications are registered before
the state update and any needed rescan, so the wallet no longer updates tx
states against a chain tip that can move without the wallet seeing the
intervening block connections.

The new test fails on the pre-fix parent (`ddb94fd3e1`) with a wallet transaction
still reporting 0 confirmations after restart, and passes on this PR head:

test/functional/wallet_chain_reprocess.py --configfile=$PWD/build/test/config.ini --timeout-factor=4

events.message:
wallet: Update tx chain state after chain notifications are attached

Updating transactions against the current chain state can only be done
in AttachChain after chain notifications have been attached. AttachChain
will guarantee that any blocks missing between the stored best block and
the current tip are rescanned, and any blocks connected during
AttachChain will be processed after loading completes.

This fixes an issue where tx states were updated with no guarantee that
any blocks connected prior to AttachChain are scanned, resulting in
incorrect tx states.
test: Check all wallet tx states are correct after unclean shutdown

events.body:
Concept ACK Moving `updateState` and coinbase abandonment from inside `LoadTxRecords`/`LoadToWallet` (during `PopulateWalletFromDB`, before the chain is attached) to `AttachChain` (after `handleNotifications` is registered) closes a real race: previously, as each tx was loaded, `updateState` queried the live chainstate — which could advance between loading tx A and tx B. This left a parent coinbase as `Inactive` while a descendant appeared `Confirmed` (its block just arrived), causing `AbandonTransaction`'s internal `try_updating_state` to hit `assert(!wtx.isConfirmed())`.
FWIW, I made some plain ASCII draw to show the code move and help me understand the flow.
BEFORE change --- ``` LoadExisting() ├─ PopulateWalletFromDB() [cs_wallet held] │ └─ WalletBatch::LoadWallet() │ └─ LoadTxRecords() │ ├─ Loop 1: LoadToWallet() × N txs │ │ └─ updateState() per tx ← ⚠ chain can move between txs │ └─ Loop 2: AbandonTransaction() ← ⚠ assert crash window for inactive coinbases ├─ TopUpKeyPool() └─ AttachChain() ├─ handleNotifications() ← register (too late) ├─ SetLastBlockProcessedInMem └─ ScanForWalletTransactions ``` AFTER change --- ``` LoadExisting() ├─ PopulateWalletFromDB() [cs_wallet held] │ └─ WalletBatch::LoadWallet() │ └─ LoadTxRecords() │ └─ Loop 1: LoadToWallet() × N txs (no updateState) ├─ TopUpKeyPool() └─ AttachChain() [cs_wallet held] ├─ handleNotifications() ← register FIRST ├─ SetLastBlockProcessedInMem ├─ Loop (reverse): updateState() + AbandonTransaction() ← consistent snapshot └─ ScanForWalletTransactions ```

comments.body:
> updating the state based on the chain data prior to AttachChain results in some blocks being missed

I believe the broad reason is to make the processing of few blocks by the wallet to be missed (on master without the fix here). Ultimately, this can happen as long as there are enough blocks for the node to process (post an unclean shutdown) so that block processing keeps on happening even after the loading of wallet (for the sync_all to come into effect).

For which I think a lower number can also be sufficient - 100 works on my system. I checked it by comparing the node's chain height right before the sync_all call on line 56 and the node's chain height before the unclean shutdown - it showed a more than 50 block difference.

Either way, it would be very helpful to mention the reason as a comment in the test here for review and future reference.

comments.body: Since the tests run with `-unsafesqlitesync`, not all data will be flushed at any given time. While we don't currently `fsync` everything on a wallet close (we probably should though), unloading the wallet at least calls `sqlite3_close` which should help to guarantee that all of the wallet data is persisted. My main concern is that killing the process while the wallet is loaded might result in data loss which could cause the test to fail intermittently or behave unexepctedly. Unloading the wallet should help mitigate such issues.

just noticed that there's no `AssertLockHeld` in `AbandonTransaction(CWalletTx&)`: this new call site in `AttachChain` relies on `cs_wallet` being held (which it is), but the overload doesn't assert it; this is pre-existing to this PR but I think worth noting...

`updateState` runs before the rescan: after an unclean shutdown, txs in blocks above the restart tip get temporarily demoted to Inactive, then the rescan/blockConnected re-confirms them. I think a comment explaining this ordering dependency perhaps would help future readers (?).

iterating children before parents ensures that descendants have `updateState` called before the parent coinbase's `AbandonTransaction` cascade reaches them — if it didn't, the chain could have advanced between processing parent and child, leaving the child Confirmed and triggering the [assert](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/c36ffd870e8b0b9933f991dc6eda661a943f3819/src/wallet/wallet.cpp#L1317).
this might be obvious... change is safe for `bitcoin-wallet` tool, since it won't call `AttachChain` either (where `updateState`'s call is being moved)...
